newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL'S BANCO NACIONAL LOSS 9.2 BLN REAIS-PAPERS.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL'S BANCO NACIONAL LOSS 9.2 BLN REAIS-PAPERS.

text.p: Losses at failed Brazilian bank Banco Nacional totaled 9.2 billion reais, according to a final report by the federal police after several months of investigations, local newspapers reported on Wednesday.
The federal police was investigating allegations that Banco Nacional, which was among Brazil's top 10 banks, had hidden huge losses by manipulating its balance sheets over a 10-year period.
The alleged fraud led the country's Central Bank to intervene in Nacional in November 1995 and sell the bank's healthy assets to private bank Unibanco .
The police also indicted 39 people, including bank directors and shareholders, on fraud charges in connection with Nacional's failure, Brazilian newspapers said.

The list of people charged with fraudulent management includes Ana Lucia Magalhaes Pinto, daughter-in-law of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and former vice-president of Nacional's council, and three other members of the Magalhaes Pinto family, which controlled the bank, the papers said.
